svg.title: The eight-item acceptance checklist for Layer 3 design, with the proof required for each item
svg.desc: Eight numbered checklist rows, each giving the item and the evidence that satisfies it. One, adjacency on both ends, proven by the neighbour state on both routers rather than one. Two, identical databases, proven by comparing link-state counts and checksums across the area. Three, symmetric link cost, proven by printing the cost on both ends of every link in the diagram. Four, summaries paired with a null0 route, proven by looking up the summary prefix and finding null0 among the entries. Five, redistribution direction, tag and seed metric written down and verified in both domains. Six, failure actually tested, proven by shutting every link and measuring recovery against the target. Seven, the convergence budget implemented, with detection, throttling and summarization all matching the document. Eight, documentation matching the device for values that are configuration rather than negotiation. A closing note says acceptance must be performed by someone who did not build the network, because the builder already believes it works.
svg.text: Eight items to prove before the design is called finished
Each row has an item and the evidence; a configuration that exists is not evidence
ITEM
EVIDENCE THAT SATISFIES IT
Adjacency on both ends
Neighbour state read on both routers. One end full and the other not is the single
most common false pass in every technology in this chapter.
Identical databases
LSA or LSP count and checksum compared across the area. A difference means two
topologies exist, and forwarding will follow the disagreement.
Symmetric cost per link
Cost printed on both ends of every link in the topology diagram. A mismatch is a
reference bandwidth or an override problem, and it produces asymmetric paths.
Every summary has null0
Look up each summary prefix and confirm null0 appears among the entries. Without
it, a dead member subnet is a silent black hole inside the area.
Redistribution is written down
Direction, tag, seed metric and filter listed per boundary, then verified from both
domains. An undocumented boundary is an outage waiting for a change window.
Failure tested, not configured
Every link shut, every process restarted, recovery measured against the target. A path
design that has never failed over is a hypothesis.
Convergence budget implemented
Detection, throttling, summarization and hierarchy all match the numbers in the
document. If there is no number in the document, there is no budget.
Documentation equals device
For values that are configuration rather than negotiation: IS-IS NET, level and metric
style, OSPF reference bandwidth, area types. Nothing corrects these for you.
Who runs the acceptance: someone who did not build the network. The builder already believes it works —
and belief is exactly the thing these eight items exist to replace with evidence.
